page: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a fixed clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated physical cores mapped to 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, providing deterministic CPU access. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage includes a 644 GB solid-state drive (SSD), while hardware GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded throughput balanced against moderate single-thread execution speed. The instance achieves 28,887.7 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 9,559.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluation, both falling squarely in the average performance tier for its core class. In contrast, Geekbench single-core performance (1,108.0) and PassMark encryption (2,591.19) indicate weaker per-core capability compared to high-frequency x86 alternatives. High sustained multi-threaded memory bandwidth (129.87 GB/sec for uncached read blocks) supports heavy in-memory execution, verified by 22.06 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.95 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the dedicated core architecture eliminates hyper-threading contention and delivers strong cost efficiency for scale-out compute. However, software workloads requiring x86 instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 or specialized vector operations will require recompilation or code adjustments for the ARM64 instruction set. The local 644 GB SSD delivers low-latency scratch space without incurring network storage overhead.

The D16pds_v5 is suitable for cloud-native web serving, software build pipelines, distributed database nodes, caching layers like Redis, and containerized microservices that benefit from uniform ARM-based core performance.
